summary: Conditional automorphy lifting for GL_n over an arbitrary number field in defect l_0 = r_1⌊(n−1)/2⌋ + r_2(n−1), after Part 2 of Calegari–Geraghty and the conditional GL_n machinery restated in the Calegari–Geraghty–Harris appendix. BT.0 defines the Taylor–Wiles-level Hecke algebras of Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_n (Definition 9.1, extended to intermediate covers), the Iwahori character local systems, the Taylor–Wiles projector and Serre modularity of minimal level. BT.1 instantiates the Galois side: a standing datum whose Ihara-avoidance set splits into places where r̄ is trivial and places with a single unipotent block (repairing Lemma 8.2), the local rings R^1_loc and R^χ_loc, the data S_Q, and the numerical coincidence of Proposition 8.5. BT.2 states Conjecture B as named hypotheses, with the added Taylor–Wiles compatibility clause, dévissage, the surjection R_{S_Q} ↠ T^an and the small-rank cases. BT.3 proves condition (5) for n = 2 (Lemma 9.6) and records the distinct-eigenvalue route of §9.4. BT.4 builds the complexes D̃_N and the two patching data and verifies the patching hypotheses; BT.5 patches, proves Theorem 9.19 (near faithfulness), minimal R = T when the local rings are smooth, cuspidal recognition, and writes the deduction of Theorem 5.16 in corrected form. Patching algebra, local and global deformation theory, locally symmetric spaces and Hecke images are imported from their owners.

nodes.title: The local systems O(ψ) of Iwahori characters
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, G = Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_n with n ≥ 2, p > n a prime, O the ring of integers of a finite extension K/ℚ_p with uniformizer ϖ and residue field k, and R a finite set of finite places of F prime to p. For v ∈ R let Iw(v) ⊂ PGL_n(O_v) be the Iwahori subgroup (upper triangular mod ϖ_v) and Iw_1(v) its pro-v radical, so Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) ≅ (k_v^×)^n/k_v^× (diagonal entries modulo scalars). An Iwahori character datum is ψ = (ψ_v)_{v∈R}, ψ_v = ψ_{v,1} × ⋯ × ψ_{v,n} : (k_v^×)^n → 1 + 𝔪_O with ∏_i ψ_{v,i} = 1, so that ψ_v factors through Iw(v)/Iw_1(v). For a level K whose component at v ∈ R is Iw(v), O(ψ) is the rank-one local system on Y(K) = G(ℚ)\G(𝔸)/K^0_∞K whose sections over U are the locally constant f on the preimage of U in Y(K ∩ ∏_{v∈R}Iw_1(v)) with f(γu) = ψ(γ)f(u) for γ ∈ ∏_{v∈R}Iw(v)/Iw_1(v). Write H^i_ψ(Y(K), A) := H^i(Y(K), O(ψ) ⊗_O A) and H_{i,ψ} for homology.
hypotheses: n ≥ 2; v ∈ R are finite places prime to p
ψ_{v,i} take values in 1 + 𝔪_O, so they have p-power order and are trivial unless p | N(v) − 1
The product condition ∏_i ψ_{v,i} = 1 is what makes ψ_v a character of the PGL_n Iwahori quotient
proofSteps: The quotient Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) is the torus of PGL_n over k_v; a character of (k_v^×)^n trivial on the diagonal k_v^× descends to it.
O(ψ) is the arithmetic local system attached to the smooth O[K]-module O on which K acts through K → ∏_{v∈R}Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) and ψ (ALS.1 arithmetic-local-system).
Cohomology and homology with coefficients in O(ψ) ⊗ A are computed by the Betti complexes of ALS.1, with coefficient change along O → A.
acceptance: For ψ = 1, O(ψ) is the constant local system O and H^*_ψ = H^*.
Since every ψ_{v,i} ≡ 1 mod ϖ, O(ψ)/ϖ is the constant local system k.
The dual local system is O(ψ^{-1}).

sources.match: The character ψ of the Iwahori quotient and the local system O(ψ) on the arithmetic quotients, with H^i_ψ and H_{i,ψ}, are defined there; trivial ψ gives O.
The homology side must use the dual local system O(χ^{-1}); recorded here as part of the API.

nodes.title: Hecke operators T_{α,k}, V_x and diamond operators at Taylor–Wiles level
nodes.statement: Keep the notation of BT.0/iwahori-character-local-system, and let Q be a finite set of finite places disjoint from S_p ∪ R with K_Q ⊃ L_Q the Taylor–Wiles levels of ALS.0/standard-level-subgroups (hyperspecial at every place outside R ∪ Q, including those above p; Iwahori at R; at x ∈ Q the line-stabilizer K_0(x) and its normal subgroup K_1(x) with K_0(x)/K_1(x) ≅ k_x^×). For K one of K_Q, L_Q or an intermediate level L_Q ⊆ K′ ⊆ K_Q, and g ∈ G(𝔸^∞) trivial at every place of R, T(g) is the correspondence H^*_ψ(Y(K)) → H^*_ψ(Y(K ∩ gKg^{-1})) → H^*_ψ(Y(g^{-1}Kg ∩ K)) → H^*_ψ(Y(K)) (pullback, translation by g, trace), with the same formula on homology. For α ∈ 𝔸_F^{∞,×} and 1 ≤ k ≤ n, T_{α,k} := T(diag(α, …, α, 1, …, 1)) with k entries α. For a prime λ ∉ S_Q, T_{λ,k} := T_{α,k} with α a uniformizer at λ and 1 elsewhere: this is the unnormalized operator, the characteristic function of K diag(ϖ_λ^{(k)}, 1^{(n−k)}) K. For x ∈ Q, V_x := T_{x,1}, well defined up to diamond operators. For δ ∈ Δ̃_Q := K_Q/L_Q ≅ ∏_{x∈Q} k_x^× the diamond operator ⟨δ⟩ acts on H^*_ψ(Y_1(Q)) as a deck transformation of Y_1(Q) → Y_0(Q); for α ∈ ∏_{x∈Q}O_x^×, T_{α,1} acts through the class of α in Δ̃_Q.
hypotheses: g trivial at R so that the correspondence preserves O(ψ)
No normalization by powers of N(λ) (sourceIssues E180 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18)

Δ̃_Q is identified with ∏ k_x^× by g ≡ (a ∗; 0 B) ↦ det(B)·a^{1−n} (ALS.0/standard-level-subgroups (iii)–(iv) give K_0(x)/K_1(x) ≅ k_x^×; this explicit map is the one fixed in sourceIssues E181 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18)
proofSteps: The correspondences and their composition law are ALS.3 (hecke-operator-formula, hecke-composition); they lift to the derived category (ALS.3/derived-hecke-action).
At λ ∉ S_Q the T_{λ,k} commute and generate the spherical Hecke algebra; IHG.3/gln-hecke-polynomial fixes the polynomial convention.

For α ∈ ∏ O_x^× the element diag(α,1,…,1) lies in K_Q, so T_{α,1} is the deck transformation by its class; with the identification above that class is α^{1−n}, and since p > n the T_{α,1} run over the p-part of Δ̃_Q.
acceptance: T_{α,k} for α ≡ 1 at all finite places is the identity.
On H^*(Y(K_∅)) with n = 2, T_{λ,1} is the classical T_λ and T_{λ,2} the diamond-type operator ⟨λ⟩ (trivial on PGL_2).
T_{λ,n} = 1 on PGL_n since diag(ϖ,…,ϖ) is central.

nodes.title: The Hecke algebras T^an_{Q,ψ} and T_{Q,ψ} (Definition 9.1)
nodes.statement: With Q and ψ as above, let 𝒦_Q be the set of levels K′ with L_Q ⊆ K′ ⊆ K_Q. T^an_{Q,ψ} is the O-subalgebra of End_O(⊕_{K′∈𝒦_Q} ⊕_{k,m} H^k_ψ(Y(K′), O/ϖ^m)) generated by the T_{α,k} (1 ≤ k ≤ n) with α a unit at every place of S_Q = S_p ∪ R ∪ Q. T_{Q,ψ} is the O-algebra generated by T^an_{Q,ψ} and the V_x = T_{x,1}, x ∈ Q, together with the diamond operators. Write T_ψ := T_{∅,ψ} = T^an_{∅,ψ} and T := T_1. Both are finite O-algebras, hence semilocal and the products of their completions at maximal ideals; for a maximal ideal m, T^an_{Q,ψ,m} is finite (not necessarily flat) over O. Two maximal ideals of T_{Q,ψ} give rise to the same Galois representation when they have the same contraction to T^an_{Q,ψ}.
hypotheses: Hecke operators as in BT.0/tw-hecke-operators
The direct sum runs over every intermediate level between L_Q and K_Q; this is the form needed in §9.5 (see sourceIssues E1 of this packet)
Coefficients O/ϖ^m for all m ≥ 1, so the algebra acts on every finite coefficient cohomology group (CG18 Remark 9.2)
proofSteps: The algebra generated by commuting operators on a finite O-module is a finite commutative O-algebra (IHG.2/cohomology-hecke-image applied to the Betti complexes of ALS.1, which have finite cohomology).
Finite algebras over the complete local ring O decompose as the product of their localizations at maximal ideals (IHG.2/finite-hecke-local-factors).

The restriction of the action to a single level K′ gives the image algebra of that level as a quotient of T^an_{Q,ψ}; pullback and trace between levels are Hecke equivariant for operators prime to S_Q.
acceptance: For Q = ∅ the set 𝒦_Q is {K_∅} and T^an_{∅,ψ} is the anemic algebra of CG18 Definition 9.1.
T^an_{Q,ψ} acts on H^*_ψ(Y_Δ(Q), O/ϖ^m) for every quotient Δ of Δ̃_Q.
For F = ℚ, n = 2 and level one, T^an_{∅,1} = O acting on H^0 by T_{λ,1} = 1 + λ.

In practice T = T^an[U_x : x ∈ Q]; two maximal ideals give the same Galois representation iff they contract to the same ideal of T^an.
The proof uses an action on H^*(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_M), O/ϖ^n)_m for the intermediate covers, which is why the algebra here includes every intermediate level.

nodes.title: The Taylor–Wiles maximal ideal m_Q and projector e_Q
nodes.statement: Let m be a maximal ideal of T^an_{Q,ψ} with residue field k. For each x ∈ Q fix a factorization P_x(X) = (X − α_x)Q_x(X) in k[X] of a monic polynomial of degree n with Q_x(α_x) ≠ 0. In the application P_x is the characteristic polynomial of r̄(Frob_x) for the residual representation r̄ of a standing datum (BT.1/ihara-avoidance-data), r̄|G_x ≅ s̄_x ⊕ ψ̄_x with ψ̄_x a one-dimensional generalized Frobenius eigenspace, and α_x := ψ̄_x(Frob_x). m_Q is the maximal ideal of T_{Q,ψ} generated by m and the V_x − α̃_x (x ∈ Q), for any lifts α̃_x ∈ O. The Taylor–Wiles projector is e_Q := lim_{k→∞} ∏_{x∈Q} Q̃_x(V_x)^{k!}, with Q̃_x any lift of Q_x to O[X]. On every finite T_{Q,ψ}-module M supported above m it is the idempotent projecting onto ⊕_𝔫 M_𝔫, the sum over the maximal ideals 𝔫 of T_{Q,ψ} above m at which no V_x is congruent to a root of Q_x; when the residual eigenvalues of every V_x on M are roots of P_x, this is the localization M_{m_Q}.
hypotheses: α_x a simple root of P_x, as for the one-dimensional generalized eigenspace ψ̄_x at a Taylor–Wiles prime (BT.1/numerical-coincidence)
Limits are in the profinite topology of the finite O-algebra T_{Q,ψ,m}
proofSteps: By IHG.2/factorial-localizing-idempotent, for t ∈ T_{Q,ψ,m} the powers t^{k!} converge to the idempotent which is 1 on the local factors where t is a unit and 0 where t lies in the maximal ideal.

Q̃_x(V_x) is a unit exactly on the local factors 𝔫 where V_x mod 𝔫 is not a root of Q_x. These include the factors where V_x ≡ α_x, since Q_x(α_x) ≠ 0, and they are exactly those factors when the residual eigenvalues of V_x are roots of P_x. For n = 2 at a Taylor–Wiles prime the m-part may a priori contain a factor with V_x ≡ ±1, which e_Q keeps; this is why Lemma 9.6 localizes at m̃ = (m, U_x − α_x) (E229 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18).

The product over x ∈ Q of these commuting idempotents is the idempotent of the factors described in the statement (the m_Q-factor under the eigenvalue condition); it commutes with diamond operators and with the T^an_{Q,ψ}-action.
acceptance: For Q = ∅, m_Q = m and e_Q = 1.
For n = 2, e_Q = lim ∏(V_x − β̃_x)^{k!} with β_x the other eigenvalue (CG18 §7.1, p. 395).
The definition is independent of the lifts α̃_x and Q̃_x.

nodes.title: Residual independence of the Iwahori character and the dual local system
nodes.statement: Let χ = (χ_v)_{v∈R} be an Iwahori character datum. (1) For every level K with Iwahori components at R, O(χ) ⊗ k ≅ k, giving H^*_χ(Y(K), k) ≅ H^*(Y(K), k) and H_{*,χ}(Y(K), k) ≅ H_*(Y(K), k), equivariantly for every Hecke operator T(g) with g trivial at R and for diamond operators. (2) Consequently each maximal ideal m of T_1 determines a maximal ideal of T_χ (also written m) with the same residual Hecke eigenvalues, and r̄_m (when Conjecture B gives it) is the same for both. (3) Under B(4)(b) at m, H^*_χ(Y(K), O/ϖ^m)^∨_m ≅ H_{*,χ^{-1}}(Y(K), O/ϖ^m)_{m^*}, where m^* is the dual maximal ideal (Remark 9.5) and the homology uses the dual local system O(χ^{-1}).
hypotheses: χ_{v,i} take values in 1 + 𝔪_O
For (3): boundary vanishing at m (Conjecture B(4)(b)) and Poincaré–Verdier duality on Y(K)
proofSteps: (1) O(χ) ⊗_O k is the constant sheaf since χ ≡ 1 mod ϖ (BT.0/iwahori-character-local-system), and the Hecke correspondences on both sides are given by the same pullback, translation and trace.
(2) The isomorphism of (1) intertwines the generators T_{α,k}, so the residual systems of eigenvalues agree; Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt identify the residual representations.

(3) Duality pairs H^i_c(Y, O(χ)) with H^{d−i}(Y, O(χ^{-1})) and identifies compactly supported cohomology with homology (ALS.5 finite-level duality); boundary vanishing identifies compactly supported and ordinary cohomology at m; Hecke adjoints send m to m^*.

In (3) the local system on the homology side is O(χ^{-1}), not O(χ) (sourceIssues E207 of the extraction).
For χ = 1, (3) is CG18 Remark 9.5.

nodes.title: Serre modular of minimal level
nodes.statement: Let r̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) be continuous and absolutely irreducible, and let R(r̄) be the set of finite places v ∤ p at which r̄ is ramified. r̄ is Serre modular of minimal level if there is a maximal ideal m of T = T_{∅,1} at the level K_∅(R(r̄)) (hyperspecial outside R(r̄), Iwahori at R(r̄)) such that m is of Galois type for the Hecke polynomial of BT.0/tw-hecke-operators (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3/galois-type-maximal-ideal; this is the residual part of B^gal, BT.2/conj-b-galois-type) with residual representation r̄_m ≅ r̄ ⊗_k k(m). Equivalently, H^*(Y(K_∅(R(r̄))), k)_m ≠ 0 for a maximal ideal m whose Hecke polynomials at λ ∉ S are the characteristic polynomials of r̄(Frob_λ).
hypotheses: r̄ has at worst unipotent ramification away from p (the setting of CG18 §8.5), so that Iwahori level at R(r̄) is the minimal level; for other ramification Iwahori level is not minimal
The level at R(r̄) is Iwahori, which realizes the Serre conductor exponent n − 1 when r̄(σ_v) is a single unipotent Jordan block (the case BT.5/theorem-5-16 uses)
This is a statement about a mod p class only; no characteristic-zero lift is asserted
proofSteps: The Hecke polynomial convention is IHG.3/gln-hecke-polynomial; Galois type is IHG.3/galois-type-maximal-ideal.
The equivalence of the two formulations is Chebotarev density together with Brauer–Nesbitt (uniqueness of semisimple representations with given characteristic polynomials).
Nonvanishing of H^*(Y, k)_m is equivalent to m lying in the support of the finite T-module H^*(Y, k).
acceptance: For n = 2 and F = ℚ this is the existence of a mod p eigenform of weight 2 and level Γ_0-type at the conductor primes with the given Galois representation, the weight-2 form of Serre's conjecture.
Serre modularity of minimal level is invariant under replacing k by a finite extension.
It is not preserved by cyclic base change in general (CG18, remark after Theorem 5.16).

sources.locator: Theorem 5.16(8)(b) and the remark after it, published pp. 383–384
sources.match: Condition (8b) is only a statement about the existence of a mod p cohomology class of level N(r̄), the natural generalization of Serre's conjecture.
The proof assumes a maximal ideal m of T = T_{∅,1} with r̄_m ≅ r̄; minimal level makes the Iwahori set R the ramification set of r̄.

nodes.title: Standing residual data with an Ihara-avoidance set
nodes.statement: A standing datum consists of: a number field F of signature (r_1, r_2); an integer n ≥ 2; a prime p > n unramified in F; the ring of integers O of a finite extension K/ℚ_p with residue field k such that W(k)[1/p] contains the images of all embeddings F ↪ Q̄_p; a continuous absolutely irreducible r̄ : G_F → GL_n(k); the character ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2} : G_F → O^× (ε the p-adic cyclotomic character, ε(Frob_λ) = N(λ) for arithmetic Frobenius); and a finite set R of finite places of F, disjoint from S_p, written R = R_triv ⊔ R_reg, together with characters χ = (χ_v)_{v∈R_triv}, χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n}), χ_{v,i} : k_v^× → 1 + 𝔪_O (equivalently, characters of O_{F_v}^× trivial on 1 + 𝔭_v) pairwise distinct with ∏_i χ_{v,i} = 1, evaluated on I_v through Art_v^{-1} (sourceIssues E168 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18). It is required that: (a) for every v | p, r̄|G_v is Fontaine–Laffaille with weights {0, 1, …, n − 1} for each embedding τ (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition); (b) N(v) ≡ 1 mod p for every v ∈ R_triv (no congruence is imposed on R_reg); (c) r̄|G_v is trivial for v ∈ R_triv; (d) for v ∈ R_reg, r̄|I_v is unipotent and r̄(σ_v) is a single Jordan block, σ_v a generator of tame inertia; (e) r̄ is unramified outside S_p ∪ R; (f) r̄ is odd (balanced) at every real place v: the ±1-eigenspaces of r̄(c_v) have dimensions differing by at most one (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7/oddness-at-real-places (d)); in characteristic p > n this is the trace condition Tr r̄(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1} except when n is even and p = n + 1 (sourceIssues E164); (g) det r̄ = ε̄^{n(n−1)/2}. Put S = S_p ⊔ R and T = S_p ∪ R (the framed places); the Iwahori character datum of BT.0 is ψ = 1 or ψ = χ, with χ extended by 1 on R_reg, viewed as a character of Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) ≅ (k_v^×)^n/k_v^×.
hypotheses: The splitting R = R_triv ⊔ R_reg replaces the single set R of CG18 §8.5: Lemma 8.2 is false without (c) at the Ihara-avoidance places (sourceIssues E169, E203 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18), and (d) is the minimal-ramification case used by CGH20 §4(2)(a); the congruence (b) is needed only where the characters χ_v live, so R_reg carries none, as in CGH20 Theorem 1.2 (A.2)

χ_{v,i} are characters of the finite group k_v^× with values in the pro-p group 1 + 𝔪_O, so they have p-power order and are nontrivial only because N(v) ≡ 1 mod p (E168: a character of I_v with values in 1 + 𝔪_O need not factor through k_v^×)

Oddness at a real place is the balanced-eigenspace condition of R02.6/archimedean-adjoint-dimensions (E164 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18: the trace criterion is not equivalent to it when n is even and p = n + 1)
proofSteps: Each condition is local except (e) and (g); (a) is meaningful because p > n and F_v/ℚ_p is unramified, so the weights lie in the Fontaine–Laffaille range [0, p − 2].
Since R contains every ramified place of r̄ away from p, (c) and (d) say that at a ramified place r̄ is a single unipotent block, and at an unramified place of R it is trivial.

χ_v extended by 1 on R_reg is a tuple of characters of (k_v^×)^n with trivial product, which is the Iwahori character datum of BT.0/iwahori-character-local-system; on inertia it acts through Art_v^{-1} and O_{F_v}^× ↠ k_v^×.
acceptance: R = ∅ is allowed; then r̄ is unramified outside p.
For n = 2 and E an elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction at v and p ∤ v(Δ_E), r̄ = E[p] has v ∈ R_reg, whatever N(v) is modulo p.
A place v with r̄|G_v unramified of nonscalar Frobenius cannot be put in R.

sources.match: The standing hypotheses: p > n unramified, Fontaine–Laffaille with weights [0, …, n − 1], unipotent ramification with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p, oddness, ξ lifting det r̄, the set R and the characters χ_v.
Lemma 8.2 rests on Taylor's Ihara-avoidance computation, which needs r̄|G_v trivial at the places carrying χ_v (E169).
At bad places with r̄(σ) a single unipotent block, the unipotent ring R^1_v is the minimally ramified ring of CHT Definition 2.4.14.

nodes.title: The local deformation rings R^1_loc and R^χ_loc
nodes.statement: For a standing datum, let C_O be the category of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field k. (i) For v | p, R_v is the framed Fontaine–Laffaille deformation ring of r̄|G_v with determinant ξ|G_v and τ-weights {0, …, n − 1}; it is formally smooth over O of relative dimension n² − 1 + [F_v : ℚ_p]n(n − 1)/2. (ii) For v ∈ R_triv, R^1_v (resp. R^{χ_v}_v) is the quotient of the framed determinant-ξ lifting ring of r̄|G_v by the condition that every σ ∈ I_v has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n (resp. ∏_i(X − χ_{v,i}(Art_v^{-1}(σ)))). (iii) For v ∈ R_reg, R^1_v is the same unipotent quotient, which equals the minimally ramified ring and is formally smooth of relative dimension n² − 1. Put R^1_loc := (⊗̂_{v|p} R_v) ⊗̂ (⊗̂_{v∈R} R^1_v) and R^χ_loc := (⊗̂_{v|p} R_v) ⊗̂ (⊗̂_{v∈R_triv} R^{χ_v}_v) ⊗̂ (⊗̂_{v∈R_reg} R^1_v), completed tensor products over O. Write D_v, D^1_v, D^χ_v for the corresponding local deformation problems.
hypotheses: Standing datum of BT.1/ihara-avoidance-data
Fixed determinant ξ in every local problem
The rings R^1_v, R^χ_v are the literal quotients of the lifting ring; their O-flat quotients would break the mod ϖ identification (sourceIssues E165)
proofSteps: (i) is LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition with smoothness from L7/fontaine-laffaille-tangent-space-and-smoothness (CHT Corollary 2.4.3), with the determinant fixed by GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/fixed-determinant-rings.

(ii) are the Ihara-avoidance quotients of R08.2/ihara-avoidance-components, taken with fixed determinant: since p ∤ n and ∏χ_{v,i} = 1, twisting by n-th roots of unramified characters identifies the variable-determinant quotient with the fixed-determinant one times a formally smooth factor in one variable.

(iii) R08.2/regular-unipotent-minimally-ramified identifies the unipotent condition with the minimally ramified one when r̄(σ_v) is a single Jordan block, and R08.2/minimally-ramified-ring gives formal smoothness.
The completed tensor products exist in C_O (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/complete-coefficient-tensor).
acceptance: R^1_v/ϖ = R^{χ_v}_v/ϖ for v ∈ R_triv because χ_{v,i} ≡ 1 mod ϖ.
For R = ∅, R^1_loc = R^χ_loc = ⊗̂_{v|p}R_v is formally smooth of relative dimension |S_p|(n² − 1) + [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2.
If R_triv = ∅ then R^1_loc = R^χ_loc is formally smooth over O.

nodes.title: Lemma 8.2 in corrected form: the local rings for Ihara avoidance
nodes.statement: For a standing datum: (1) R^1_loc and R^χ_loc are equidimensional of Krull dimension 1 + |S_p ∪ R|(n² − 1) + [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2, and every minimal prime of each has characteristic 0; (2) there is a natural isomorphism R^1_loc/ϖ ≅ R^χ_loc/ϖ; (3) Spec R^χ_loc is irreducible, after enlarging O if necessary; (4) every irreducible component of Spec R^1_loc/ϖ is contained in a unique irreducible component of Spec R^1_loc. Neither ring is asserted to be p-torsion free; R^1_loc is not when R_triv ≠ ∅.
hypotheses: Standing datum with R = R_triv ⊔ R_reg (BT.1/ihara-avoidance-data); O large enough that the irreducible components of each factor are geometrically irreducible
The printed Lemma 8.2 asserts p-torsion freeness and states (3) without r̄|G_v trivial on R; both are false in that generality (E165, E169)
proofSteps: Factors at v | p and v ∈ R_reg are formally smooth over O, hence O-flat domains with irreducible generic fibre and the stated relative dimensions (BT.1/cg-local-rings).

At v ∈ R_triv, Taylor's computation (R08.2/ihara-avoidance-components, in fixed determinant): Spec R^{χ_v}_v is irreducible with generic point of characteristic 0, R^1_v/ϖ = R^{χ_v}_v/ϖ, every component of Spec R^1_v has the same dimension and characteristic-0 generic point, and each prime minimal over ϖ contains a unique minimal prime.

Completed tensor products over O of rings that are equidimensional with characteristic-0 minimal primes and geometrically irreducible components are again such, with dimensions adding (relative dimensions add), components being products of components, and the 'unique component above each special component' property preserved: this is BLGHT Lemma 3.3, requested from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3.
(1), (3), (4) follow factor by factor from the previous steps; (2) is the tensor product of the factorwise identifications mod ϖ.
acceptance: The dimension count: Σ_{v|p}(n² − 1 + [F_v : ℚ_p]n(n − 1)/2) + |R|(n² − 1) + 1 = 1 + |S_p ∪ R|(n² − 1) + [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2.
If R_triv = ∅ then R^1_loc = R^χ_loc is formally smooth, and (1)–(4) are immediate.
The counterexample of E169: with v ∈ R, r̄|G_v unramified of distinct Frobenius eigenvalues and χ_{v,2} = χ_{v,1}^{-1} ≠ χ_{v,1}, Spec R^{χ_v}_v[1/p] is disconnected; the datum excludes this v.

sources.locator: §8.5.1, Lemma 8.2 and its proof, published pp. 407–408
sources.match: Lemma 8.2 lists the four properties, citing BLGHT [76, Lemma 3.3] and Taylor [11, Proposition 3.1]; the corrected form replaces p-torsion freeness by characteristic-0 minimal primes (E165) and restricts the Ihara-avoidance places to r̄|G_v trivial (E169).
The proof uses only the dimension, irreducibility of Spec R^2_∞, the mod ϖ identification and characteristic-0 minimal primes.

nodes.title: The global deformation data S_Q and S^χ_Q
nodes.statement: For a standing datum and a finite set Q of places disjoint from S at which r̄|G_x ≅ s̄_x ⊕ ψ̄_x with ψ̄_x a one-dimensional generalized Frobenius eigenspace and N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, let D_x be the Taylor–Wiles local problem of R08.2/taylor-wiles-local-tangent: lifts of determinant ξ of the form s_x ⊕ ψ_x lifting s̄_x ⊕ ψ̄_x with I_x acting by scalars on s_x and on ψ_x. S_Q := (r̄, O, S ⊔ Q, ξ, (D_v)_{v∈S_p∪Q}, (D^1_v)_{v∈R}) and S^χ_Q := (r̄, O, S ⊔ Q, ξ, (D_v)_{v∈S_p∪Q}, (D^χ_v)_{v∈R_triv}, (D^1_v)_{v∈R_reg}) are global deformation data in the sense of GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.3/global-deformation-type. A deformation is of type S_Q if it is unramified outside S ⊔ Q, has determinant ξ, and lies in the given local problem at each v ∈ S_p ∪ Q ∪ R. R_{S_Q} and R^{□_T}_{S_Q} (T-framed) are the representing objects; S := S_∅. Restriction of the universal deformation to I_x, x ∈ Q, on the ψ_x-line gives a character of the maximal p-power quotient Δ_x of k_x^× (via Art_x), making R_{S_Q} an O[Δ_Q]-algebra, Δ_Q := ∏_{x∈Q}Δ_x, with R_{S_Q} ⊗_{O[Δ_Q]} O = R_S.
hypotheses: r̄ absolutely irreducible, so the unframed functor is representable
p ∤ n so ad r̄ = k ⊕ ad⁰ r̄
The Taylor–Wiles places carry the one-dimensional eigenspace condition of CG18 §8.5.1
proofSteps: Representability of the T-framed and unframed functors: R04.3/global-framed-ring, using that each local problem is a local deformation problem (R04.3/local-deformation-problem).
The local maps R^1_loc → R^{□_T}_{S_Q} and R^χ_loc → R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q} are R04.3/local-to-global-map.

At x ∈ Q a lift of type D_x is s_x ⊕ ψ_x, and ψ_x|I_x factors through the p-part of k_x^× since N(x) ≡ 1 mod p (the block form of R08.2/taylor-wiles-block-condition with n_1 = 1); this defines O[Δ_Q] → R_{S_Q}.
Killing the augmentation ideal forces ψ_x and s_x unramified, which with determinant ξ unramified at x gives deformations of type S (R04.4/enlarging-ramification).
acceptance: S_∅ = S and S^χ_∅ = S^χ.
R_{S_Q}/ϖ ≅ R_{S^χ_Q}/ϖ because the local problems agree mod ϖ.
The O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure agrees with GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5/taylor-wiles-inertia-action for n = 2 after the twist recorded in R08.2/taylor-wiles-block-condition.

nodes.title: Framing and presentation over the local rings (Lemma 8.3, Proposition 8.4)
nodes.statement: For a standing datum and Q as in BT.1/cg-global-deformation-data: (1) R_{S_Q} → R^{□_T}_{S_Q} is formally smooth of relative dimension n²|T| − 1 (and likewise for S^χ_Q), for T nonempty. (2) R^{□_T}_{S_Q} (resp. R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q}) is a quotient of a power series ring over R^1_loc (resp. R^χ_loc) in h¹_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad⁰r̄) + Σ_{v∈T} h⁰(G_v, ad r̄) − h⁰(G_F, ad r̄) variables, where H¹_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad⁰r̄) is the kernel of H¹(G_{F,S_Q}, ad⁰r̄) → ⊕_{x∈T} H¹(G_x, ad⁰r̄) ⊕ ⊕_{x∈Q} H¹(G_x, ad⁰r̄)/L_x. (3) h¹_{L(Q),T}(ad⁰r̄) = h¹_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(ad⁰r̄(1)) + h⁰(G_F, ad⁰r̄) − h⁰(G_F, ad⁰r̄(1)) + Σ_{x∈Q}(dim L_x − h⁰(G_x, ad⁰r̄)) − Σ_{v∈T∪{v|∞}} h⁰(G_v, ad⁰r̄).
hypotheses: T = S_p ∪ R nonempty (it contains the places above p)
r̄ absolutely irreducible and p ∤ n
proofSteps: (1) The T-framed functor is a torsor over the formal group (∏_{v∈T} Γ̂_n)/Ĝ_m of framings: GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/framed-unframed-comparison in its T-framed form (G8/variable-determinant-representability gives the n²|T| − 1 count for nonempty T).

(2) R04.3/local-to-global-presentation: the relative tangent space of R^{□_T}_{S_Q} over the local ring is the Selmer group relative to T, corrected by the framing variables Σ_{v∈T}h⁰(G_v, ad r̄) − h⁰(G_F, ad r̄) (R04.3/relative-tangent-space).
(3) Poitou–Tate duality and the Greenberg–Wiles formula (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5/greenberg-wiles-formula) for M = ad⁰r̄ with conditions 0 at T, L_x at Q and unramified elsewhere.
acceptance: With Q = ∅ and R = ∅, (3) reads h¹_{∅,S_p}(ad⁰) = h¹_{⊥}(ad⁰(1)) − Σ_{v|p}h⁰(G_v, ad⁰) − Σ_{v|∞}h⁰(G_v, ad⁰) when h⁰(ad⁰) = h⁰(ad⁰(1)) = 0.
For n = 1, ad⁰ r̄ = 0 and (3) reads 0 = 0; the rank-one count of BT.1/gl1-defect-example uses ad r̄ = k instead (R02.5/rank-one-selmer-numerics).
(1) fails for T = ∅: the unframed ring is not a power series ring over itself in −1 variables.

sources.match: Lemma 8.3 (relative dimension n²|T| − 1) and Proposition 8.4 (number of variables over R^1_loc and the Euler characteristic identity), proved by the argument of Kisin's Lemma 3.2.2 and Poitou–Tate.

nodes.title: The numerical coincidence (Proposition 8.5)
nodes.statement: For a standing datum with r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) big (CHT Definition 2.5.1) and F(ad⁰r̄) ∌ ζ_p, and an integer q ≥ h¹_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad⁰r̄(1)), for every N ≥ 1 there is a tuple (Q, (ψ̄_x)_{x∈Q}) with: (1) |Q| = q and Q ∩ S = ∅; (2) r̄|G_x ≅ s̄_x ⊕ ψ̄_x with ψ̄_x a one-dimensional generalized Frobenius eigenspace; (3) N(x) ≡ 1 mod p^N; (4) R^{□_T}_{S_Q} (resp. R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q}) is a quotient of R^1_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧ (resp. R^χ_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧) with g = q + |T| − 1 − [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 − l_0, l_0 = r_1⌊(n − 1)/2⌋ + r_2(n − 1). Consequently, with j = n²|T| − 1, dim R^1_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧ = 1 + q + j − l_0.
hypotheses: r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) big in the sense of CHT Definition 2.5.1 (requested from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7) and F(ad⁰r̄) ∌ ζ_p
r̄ odd at the real places, so that the archimedean count of R02.6 applies
N(x) ≡ 1 mod p for x ∈ Q is what gives dim_k L_x − h⁰(G_x, ad⁰r̄) = 1 (R08.2/taylor-wiles-local-tangent)
proofSteps: (1)–(3) and the vanishing H¹_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad⁰r̄(1)) = 0: choose x by Chebotarev so that each class of the dual Selmer group is detected by tr(e_x φ(Frob_x)), as in CHT Proposition 2.5.9; this rank-n big-image selection is requested from GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5.

Then BT.1/framing-and-presentation (2)–(3) with h¹_{L(Q)^⊥,T} = 0, h⁰(G_F, ad⁰) = h⁰(G_F, ad⁰(1)) = 0 (absolute irreducibility and ζ_p ∉ F(ad⁰r̄)), dim L_x − h⁰ = 1 at x ∈ Q, h⁰(G_v, ad) = h⁰(G_v, ad⁰) + 1 (p ∤ n), and Σ_{v|∞}h⁰(G_v, ad⁰) = [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 + l_0 (R02.6/archimedean-adjoint-dimensions, using oddness) give g = q + |T| − 1 − [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 − l_0.
Adding dim R^1_loc = 1 + |T|(n² − 1) + [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 (BT.1/local-ring-properties) to g gives 1 + q + (n²|T| − 1) − l_0.
acceptance: For F imaginary quadratic and n = 2, l_0 = 1, [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 = 2 and g = q + |T| − 4.
For F totally real and n = 2, l_0 = 0, recovering the Taylor–Wiles–Kisin count g = q + |T| − 1 − [F:ℚ].
For n = 1 the formula gives l_0 = r_1 + r_2 − 1 only with the GL_1 conventions of BT.1/gl1-defect-example, not the PGL_n formula, which gives 0.

sources.locator: §8.6, Proposition 8.5 and its proof, published pp. 410–411
sources.match: Choice of q Taylor–Wiles primes killing the dual Selmer group (via CHT Proposition 2.5.9) and the count q + |T| − 1 − [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 − l_0 of variables.
Σ_{v|∞} dim H⁰(F_v, ad⁰V) = [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 + l_0 for odd V.
Checks 1 + (n² − 1)|T| + [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 + g = 1 + j + q − l_0 with j = n²|T| − 1.

nodes.title: Lifts satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 5.16 have type S
nodes.statement: Let (F, n, p, O, r̄, R) be a standing datum and r : G_F → GL_n(O′) (O′ ⊇ O finite) a continuous lift of r̄ such that: r is unramified outside S; for v | p, r|G_v is crystalline with gr^i(r ⊗ B_dR)^{G_v} free of rank one over O ⊗ F_v for i ∈ {0, …, n − 1} and zero otherwise; for v ∈ R, r|I_v is unipotent; det r = ε^{n(n−1)/2}. Then r is a deformation of r̄ of type S, hence defines an O-algebra map x_r : R_S → O′ whose kernel is a prime of R_S with residue ring O′.
hypotheses: p > n unramified in F, so the Hodge–Tate weights lie in the Fontaine–Laffaille range [0, p − 2]
Standing datum (BT.1/ihara-avoidance-data); the determinant convention ε(Frob_λ) = N(λ)
proofSteps: At v | p: a crystalline representation of an unramified p-adic field with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p − 2] has Fontaine–Laffaille lattices, and the weights {0, …, n − 1} with multiplicity one per embedding identify r|G_v with an O′-point of R_v (PadicHodgeTheory R06.4/fontaine-laffaille-crystalline-comparison, LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition).

At v ∈ R: unipotent inertia means every σ ∈ I_v has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n, the defining condition of R^1_v; on R_reg this is the minimally ramified ring (R08.2/regular-unipotent-minimally-ramified).
det r = ξ and unramifiedness outside S are the remaining conditions of type S; the deformation class of r gives x_r by representability (BT.1/cg-global-deformation-data).
acceptance: An O′-point of R_S is the same as a deformation of type S over O′.
If r is ramified at v ∈ R_triv, x_r lies on a component of R^1_v other than the unramified one.
A lift with r|I_v of infinite order but non-unipotent is not of type S.

sources.match: The local hypotheses on r: crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights {0, …, n − 1}, unipotent ramification and determinant ε^{n(n−1)/2}.

sources.locator: §9.5, published p. 424 (with the review note: corollary remark)
sources.match: Theorem 5.16 is said to follow immediately from Theorem 9.19; the step that r is of type S is not written (brief of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18, item thm-5-16).

nodes.title: The case GL_1: defect l_0 = r_1 + r_2 − 1 and class field theory
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field with ζ_p ∉ F and r̄ : G_F → k^× the trivial character. Minimal deformations are the everywhere unramified characters, with universal ring R^unr. The arithmetic quotients X_Q = F^×\𝔸_F^×/U_Q A^0_∞ of GL_1 have components which are compact tori of dimension l_0 = r_1 + r_2 − 1, and the dimension of the dual Selmer group to be killed exceeds that of the Selmer group by the same l_0. Patching complexes of length l_0 gives R^unr ≅ ℤ_p[Cl(O_F) ⊗ ℤ_p], i.e. the p-part of the Hilbert class field corresponds to the p-part of the class group. The argument is circular: the Greenberg–Wiles formula it uses rests on class field theory.
hypotheses: ζ_p ∉ F (otherwise the choice of auxiliary primes fails)
The PGL_n formula for l_0 does not specialize to this case; GL_1 has its own l_0 = r_1 + r_2 − 1
proofSteps: dim H¹_L(F, F_p) − dim H¹_{L*}(F, μ_p) = −(r_1 + r_2 − 1): ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5/rank-one-selmer-numerics.
Each component of X_Q has dimension r_1 + r_2 − 1 (AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.5/gl1-component-dimension), so its cohomology lives in degrees [0, l_0].
Taylor–Wiles primes are primes with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^N at which the Kummer classes of a basis of the dual Selmer group are nontrivial; they exist by Chebotarev because ζ_p ∉ F.

The Hecke action on H^0 is through the ray class group by class field theory and propagates to higher degrees by Künneth; patching then identifies R^unr with the group algebra of the p-part of the class group.
acceptance: l_0 = r_1 + r_2 − 1 equals the number of excess dual Selmer classes.
For F = ℚ, l_0 = 0 and the statement is R^unr = ℤ_p (no unramified p-extension of ℚ).
For F imaginary quadratic, l_0 = 0 as well; for F real quadratic, l_0 = 1.

sources.match: The one-dimensional case: Greenberg–Wiles count −(r_1 + r_2 − 1), the spaces X_Q as products of circles, choice of auxiliary primes using ζ_p ∉ F, the conclusion R^unr ≅ ℤ_p[Cl(O_F) ⊗ ℤ_p], and the remark that the argument is circular.

nodes.title: Conjecture B, residual and integral Galois representations (hypothesis)
nodes.statement: For Q, ψ as in BT.0 and a maximal ideal m of T^an_{Q,ψ}, the hypothesis B^gal(Q, ψ, m) is the conjunction of: (i) there is a continuous semisimple r̄_m : G_F → GL_n(T^an_{Q,ψ}/m), unramified outside S_Q, such that for every prime λ ∉ S_Q the characteristic polynomial of r̄_m(Frob_λ) (arithmetic Frobenius) is X^n − T_{λ,1}X^{n−1} + ⋯ + (−1)^i N(λ)^{i(i−1)/2}T_{λ,i}X^{n−i} + ⋯ + (−1)^n N(λ)^{n(n−1)/2}T_{λ,n} in (T^an_{Q,ψ}/m)[X], with the unnormalized T_{λ,i}; that is, m is of Galois type in the sense of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants (IHG.3/galois-type-maximal-ideal) for this Hecke polynomial; (ii) if r̄_m is absolutely irreducible (m non-Eisenstein), there is a continuous lift r_m : G_F → GL_n(T^an_{Q,ψ,m}) of r̄_m, unramified outside S_Q, whose characteristic polynomials at Frob_λ, λ ∉ S_Q, are given by the same formula in T^an_{Q,ψ,m}[X]. It is a hypothesis: a named proposition assumed by the theorems of BT.5, never asserted.
hypotheses: The unnormalized T_{λ,i} of BT.0/tw-hecke-operators (with the printed normalization the exponent would have to be i(i+1)/2; E180)
Arithmetic Frobenius; IHG.3/frobenius-conversion converts to geometric Frobenius
proofSteps: (i) determines r̄_m up to isomorphism by Chebotarev density and Brauer–Nesbitt (IHG.3/galois-type-maximal-ideal, uniqueness).

When r̄_m is absolutely irreducible, a lift as in (ii) is unique up to conjugation by Carayol's theorem (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem), and is equivalent to a continuous determinant G_F → T^an_{Q,ψ,m} with the given characteristic polynomials (IHG.1 reconstruction).
acceptance: For F = ℚ and n = 2, (i) and (ii) hold at every non-Eisenstein m by Eichler–Shimura, Deligne and Carayol.
For F CM, (i) holds by Scholze, and (ii) holds modulo a nilpotent ideal; the full (ii) over T^an_m is not known in general.
At an Eisenstein m with r̄_m = 1 ⊕ ε̄ (n = 2), (i) holds and (ii) is not asked.

sources.match: Predicts semisimple r̄_m with the stated Frobenius characteristic polynomials, defines non-Eisenstein by absolute irreducibility, and predicts the deformation r_m over T^an_{Q,ψ,m}.
Conjecture B of CG18 consists of five parts; the appendix assumes all but (4).

uses.how: r_m is the deformation that gives R_{S_Q} ↠ T^an_{Q,ψ,m}
r̄_m(G_{F(ζ_p)}) big excludes residual eigensystems
assumed for GL_n over CM fields

nodes.title: Conjecture B(1)–(3) and the Taylor–Wiles compatibility (6) (hypothesis)
nodes.statement: Assume B^gal(Q, ψ, m) with m non-Eisenstein, r̄_m ≅ r̄ ⊗ T^an/m for the r̄ of a standing datum, and Q a set of Taylor–Wiles primes as in BT.1/numerical-coincidence (Q = ∅ allowed). B^lgc(Q, ψ, m) is the conjunction of: (1) for v | p, r_m|G_v is Fontaine–Laffaille with all weights {0, 1, …, n − 1} (an object of the deformation problem D_v of BT.1/cg-local-rings); (2) for v ∈ Q, r_m|G_v is a lifting of type D_v (r_m|G_v ≅ s_v ⊕ ψ_v with I_v acting by scalars on each summand); (3) for v ∈ R and σ ∈ I_v, the characteristic polynomial of r_m(σ) is ∏_i(X − ψ_{v,i}(Art_v^{-1}(σ))); (6) for v ∈ Q and α ∈ O_v^× (α = 1 at the other places), the operator T_{α,1} acts on H^*_ψ(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m)_m as the scalar by which r_m(Art_v(α)) acts on the lift ψ_v of the line ψ̄_v.
hypotheses: Clause (6) is not in CG18's Conjecture B; it is the GL(n) analogue of Conjecture A(3), needed for condition (d) of the patching theorem and for the surjection onto T^an including diamond operators (sourceIssues E181 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18)
Art_v normalized as in BT.0 (uniformizers to arithmetic Frobenius); on the homology side (m^*) the clause holds with the inverse character
proofSteps: (1)–(3) are the printed local–global compatibility clauses; (3) with ψ = 1 says inertia at R acts unipotently.

Under the identification K_Q/L_Q ≅ ∏k_x^× of BT.0/tw-hecke-operators, T_{α,1} has class α^{1−n}, so (6) fixes the action of O[Δ_Q] on the m-part, and p > n makes the T_{α,1} exhaust the p-part of Δ̃_Q.
acceptance: For Q = ∅ clauses (2) and (6) are empty.
For F CM, (1) is known only up to a nilpotent ideal and under extra hypotheses (ACC+, Caraiani–Newton); (2), (3) and (6) follow from local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p.
With ψ = χ, clause (3) places r_m in R^χ_v at v ∈ R_triv.

The GL_2 version includes local–global compatibility of diamond operators at Taylor–Wiles primes, the model for clause (6).

nodes.title: Conjecture B(4): vanishing outside [q_0, q_0 + l_0] and on the boundary (hypothesis)
nodes.statement: For Q, ψ and a maximal ideal m of T^an_{Q,ψ}, B^van(Q, ψ, m) is the conjunction, over every level K′ ∈ 𝒦_Q and every m ≥ 1, of: (a) H^i_ψ(Y(K′), O/ϖ^m)_m = 0 unless q_0 ≤ i ≤ q_0 + l_0; (b) H^i_ψ(∂Y(K′), O/ϖ^m)_m = 0 for all i, ∂Y(K′) the boundary of the Borel–Serre compactification. Here l_0, q_0 are the invariants of AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4/l0-q0-invariants for Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_n: l_0 = r_1⌊(n − 1)/2⌋ + r_2(n − 1) and 2q_0 + l_0 = dim Y.
hypotheses: Stated at every intermediate level, matching BT.0/tw-hecke-algebra
Cohomology of the boundary is localized for the Hecke operators prime to S_Q acting on boundary cohomology (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.4)
proofSteps: (b) and the boundary triangle (ALS.4/boundary-triangle) give H^*_c ≅ H^* after localization, and with Poincaré–Verdier duality (ALS.5) H^*(Y, O/ϖ^m)^∨_m ≅ H_*(Y, O/ϖ^m)_{m^*}.
By dévissage (BT.2/conj-b-devissage) it suffices to check m = 1.
acceptance: For F = ℚ and n = 2 (l_0 = 0, q_0 = 1), (a) says H^0 and H^2 vanish at non-Eisenstein m, which holds.
For F imaginary quadratic and n = 2 (l_0 = 1, q_0 = 1), (a) asks vanishing in degrees 0 and 3 only.
(a) is open in general; (b) follows from Galois representations for the Levi cohomology (ALS.4/gln-boundary-eisenstein) when those are available.

nodes.title: Conjecture B(5): no new cohomology at Taylor–Wiles level (hypothesis)
nodes.statement: For Q a set of Taylor–Wiles primes and m as in BT.0/tw-maximal-ideal-and-projector, B^tw(Q, ψ, m) asserts that for every m ≥ 1 the composite of pr^*, e_Q and the projection onto the m_Q-part, H^*_ψ(Y, O/ϖ^m)_m → H^*_ψ(Y_0(Q), O/ϖ^m)_{m_Q}, is an isomorphism, where pr : Y_0(Q) → Y is the natural projection and e_Q = lim_{k→∞} ∏_{x∈Q} Q_x(V_x)^{k!} is the Taylor–Wiles projector.

nodes.title: Conjecture B gives R_{S_Q} ↠ T^an_{Q,ψ,m} as O[Δ_Q]-algebras
nodes.statement: Let a standing datum be given, Q a Taylor–Wiles set, ψ ∈ {1, χ}, and m a maximal ideal of T^an_{Q,ψ} with r̄_m ≅ r̄. Assume B^gal and B^lgc at (Q, ψ, m), and ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2}. Then r_m is a deformation of r̄ of type S_Q (ψ = 1) or S^χ_Q (ψ = χ), and the induced map R_{S_Q} → T^an_{Q,1,m} (resp. R_{S^χ_Q} → T^an_{Q,χ,m}) is a surjection of O[Δ_Q]-algebras: it sends tr ρ^univ(Frob_λ) to T_{λ,1} and the inertial character at x ∈ Q to the diamond action. It is compatible with the maps between intermediate levels in 𝒦_Q and, for Q = ∅, gives R_S ↠ T_m and R_{S^χ} ↠ T_{χ,m}.
hypotheses: ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2} (the printed text leaves this implicit; E186)
Clause (6) for the Δ_Q-linearity (E181)
proofSteps: Clauses (1)–(3) of B^lgc and det r_m = ε^{n(n−1)/2} (from T_{λ,n} = 1 and Chebotarev) show r_m is of type S_Q or S^χ_Q (BT.1/cg-global-deformation-data).

The image of R_{S_Q} is the closed O-subalgebra generated by the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of r_m(Frob_λ), which are the T_{λ,i}; these generate T^an_{Q,ψ,m} together with the diamond operators.
Clause (6) identifies the diamond operators with the images of the inertial characters ψ_x, so the image contains them and the map is O[Δ_Q]-linear.
Compatibility with the maps between levels holds because pullback and trace commute with the T_{λ,i}, λ ∉ S_Q.
acceptance: For Q = ∅ this is R_S ↠ T_m, used in Theorem 9.19.
Without (6) only the subalgebra generated by the T_{λ,i} is hit, and the surjection onto T^an_{Q,ψ,m} can fail.
With ψ = χ the map lands in T^an_{Q,χ,m} and its reduction mod ϖ agrees with the ψ = 1 map under BT.0/residual-character-independence.

nodes.title: Conjecture B(4)(a) in small rank (Remark 9.3)
nodes.statement: Let m be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal at which B^gal and B^van(b) hold. (1) For F imaginary quadratic and n = 2 (dim Y = 3, l_0 = q_0 = 1), H^0(Y(K′), O/ϖ^m)_m = H^3(Y(K′), O/ϖ^m)_m = 0 for every level, so B^van(a) holds. (2) For n = 3, F = ℚ ((q_0, l_0) = (2, 1), d = dim Y = 5) and for n = 2 with F a CM field of degree 4 ((q_0, l_0) = (2, 2), d = 6), with p > n unramified in F as in the standing data, suppose also that B^gal holds at the dual maximal ideal m^∨ and that m^∨ is non-Eisenstein. Then H^i(Y(K′), O/ϖ^m)_m = 0 for i ∈ {0, 1, d − 1, d} and every level K′, so B^van(a) holds.
hypotheses: Boundary vanishing at m (B^van(b)) for the step from H_c to H, or ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.4/gln-boundary-eisenstein where Galois representations of the Levi factors are available

For (2): p > n unramified in F, so p ∤ #μ(F); the congruence-kernel theorems behind the vanishing of H^0 and H^1 (Bass–Milnor–Serre for SL_3(ℤ), Serre 1970 for SL_2(O_F) with O_F^× infinite) are planned in KTheoryLowDegrees U.4 and enter through U.4/cg-localized-h1-vanishing
In both cases of (2), G(ℝ) = PGL_3(ℝ) or PGL_2(ℂ)² is connected, so Y(K′) is orientable and Poincaré duality needs no orientation twist
proofSteps: (1) H^0 at a non-Eisenstein m vanishes because H^0(Y, k) is spanned by component classes on which T_{λ,1} acts by a degree (Eisenstein eigenvalues); H^3 = H^3_c (boundary vanishing) is dual to H^0 at m^*.

(2) KTheoryLowDegrees U.4/cg-localized-h1-vanishing gives H^0(Y(K′), k)_m = H^1(Y(K′), k)_m = 0 at every level for a non-Eisenstein m, and likewise at m^∨: a finite central congruence kernel of order prime to p makes every mod-p character of the lattices congruence, and the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre sequence then places it in Eisenstein-supported H^0.

Poincaré duality (ALS.5 verdier-poincare-duality, with hecke-adjoint-duality sending m to m^∨) identifies H_c^{d−i}(Y, k)_m with the dual of H^i(Y, k)_{m^∨}, which vanishes for i = 0, 1; boundary vanishing at m (ALS.4/boundary-triangle) identifies H_c^{d−i} and H^{d−i} after localization.
The degrees outside [q_0, q_0 + l_0] are 0, 1, d − 1, d; dévissage (BT.2/conj-b-devissage) passes from k to O/ϖ^m.
acceptance: For F imaginary quadratic the proof needs no congruence subgroup property (CG18 Lemma 5.9(1)); H^1 and H^2 lie in the range [1, 2] there.
The printed degree q_0 − 1 is d − 1 (E184); Serre's 1970 paper is the right citation for the CM quartic case (E185); KTheoryLowDegrees U.4 leaves the degree d − 1 half of Remark 9.3 to this node.
For n = 2 and F real quadratic, l_0 = 0 and q_0 = 2 (Hilbert modular surfaces), which is not covered.

nodes.title: Reduction from PGL_2 to PSL_2 arithmetic groups
nodes.statement: Let n = 2, p odd, and Y = ⊔_i Γ_i\ℋ the decomposition of an arithmetic quotient of Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_2 into components (ℋ the symmetric space, Γ_i congruence subgroups commensurable with PGL_2(O_F)). For each Γ = Γ_i put Γ^1 := Γ ∩ PSL_2(O_F). Then Φ := Γ/Γ^1 is an elementary abelian 2-group and, for every m ≥ 1, restriction gives H^*(Γ, O/ϖ^m) ≅ H^*(Γ^1, O/ϖ^m)^Φ; the same holds for Γ_0(x) and Γ^1_0(x) := Γ_0(x) ∩ Γ^1, compatibly with restriction maps and with double-coset operators from elements of PSL_2(F).
hypotheses: p odd (p > n = 2)
Component groups as in ALS.0/component-decomposition; at non-neat level the cohomology is that of the arithmetic groupoid
proofSteps: PGL_2/PSL_2 is identified with F^×/F^{×2} through the determinant, so Γ/Γ^1 embeds in O_F^×/O_F^{×2}-type groups of exponent two (ALS.0/component-decomposition).
The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for Γ^1 ⊂ Γ with |Φ| a power of 2 invertible in O/ϖ^m degenerates to the invariants (ALS.6/finite-cover-hochschild-serre, degenerate case).
Double-coset operators of elements of PSL_2(F) normalize the situation and commute with the Φ-action.
acceptance: For F = ℚ and Γ = PGL_2(ℤ), Φ = ℤ/2 and Γ^1 = PSL_2(ℤ).
The statement fails for p = 2.
Φ acts on H^*(Γ^1) through the outer action of a matrix of determinant a unit not a square.

nodes.title: The S-arithmetic amalgam G = Γ^1 ∗_{Γ^1_0(x)} Γ^1
nodes.statement: Let n = 2, x a Taylor–Wiles prime with K_x maximal, and assume x is trivial in the ray class group governing the components of Y, with π_x ∈ O_F a generator of x. For Γ^1 as in BT.3/psl2-reduction, with level maximal at x, let Γ^1_0(x) := Γ_0(x) ∩ Γ^1, h := diag(1, π_x) ∈ PGL_2(F) and g := diag(π_x, π_x^{-1}) ∈ PSL_2(F). Then Γ^1 ∩ hΓ^1h^{-1} = Γ^1_0(x), Γ^1 and hΓ^1h^{-1} being the stabilizers of two adjacent vertices of the Bruhat–Tits tree of PSL_2(F_x); the subgroup G of PSL_2(O_F[1/x]) generated by Γ^1 and hΓ^1h^{-1} is a congruence subgroup with the same level as Γ^1 away from x and contains g; and G is the amalgamated product Γ^1 ∗_{Γ^1_0(x)} Γ^1 of Γ^1 with itself along Γ^1_0(x), embedded in the first factor by inclusion and in the second by γ ↦ h^{-1}γh. G acts on the tree without inversion with an edge as fundamental domain. Conjugation by g moves a vertex to one at distance two, so Γ^1 and gΓ^1g^{-1} do not form this amalgam.
hypotheses: Without the triviality assumption on x one amalgamates different Γ_i of the component decomposition; the argument is the same with more notation
Strong approximation for SL_2 over F with respect to the place x (SL_2(F_x) noncompact)
proofSteps: Local Ihara amalgam: PSL_2(F_x) is the amalgamated product of the stabilizers of two adjacent vertices of its tree over the Iwahori subgroup (ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2/ihara-amalgam).

Strong approximation for SL_2 (AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4/strong-approximation-theorem) gives density of the S-arithmetic group in PSL_2(F_x) and identifies the quotient of the tree by G with one edge, whose vertex stabilizers are Γ^1 and hΓ^1h^{-1} and whose edge stabilizer is Γ^1_0(x); g lies in G because π_x is a unit congruent to 1 at the level away from x (the triviality of x in the ray class group).
Serre's structure theorem for groups acting on trees with an edge as quotient gives the amalgam.
acceptance: For F = ℚ and Γ^1 = PSL_2(ℤ), G = PSL_2(ℤ[1/x]) and the statement is Ihara's theorem.
G contains g, so the double coset GgG = G acts on H^*(G) as the identity (sourceIssues E189 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18).
The amalgam does not exist for PGL_2 (only for the even-valuation subgroup).

nodes.title: The operator U_{x²} on Γ^1_0(x)-cohomology
nodes.statement: With x, π_x as in BT.3/global-ihara-amalgam, U_{x²} is N(x)^{-2} times the double-coset operator of Γ^1_0(x) attached to diag(π_x², 1), equivalently (the operator depends on the matrix only up to scalars) to g = diag(π_x, π_x^{-1}). It acts on H^*(Γ^1_0(x), O/ϖ^m), on H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m) componentwise, and on H^*(G, O/ϖ^m) through the double coset GgG = G, where the unnormalized operator is the identity, so that U_{x²} acts on H^*(G) by the scalar N(x)^{-2} (not by 1 as printed; sourceIssues E189 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18). On H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m), U_x² = U_{x²} for U_x normalized as N(x)^{-1} times the double coset of diag(π_x, 1); for the unnormalized V_x = T_{x,1}, V_x² = N(x)²U_{x²} ≡ U_{x²} mod p.
hypotheses: N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, so N(x) is a unit and N(x)² ≡ 1 mod p
proofSteps: The double-coset operator [Γ^1_0(x) g Γ^1_0(x)] is defined by restriction, conjugation and corestriction (ALS.3/hecke-operator-formula).

Since g ∈ G, the double coset GgG is the single coset G and the induced endomorphism of H^*(G) is the identity (conjugation by an element of G acts trivially on H^*(G)); it is also the map induced on H_0 of the Bruhat–Tits tree by the compatible endomorphism of its chain complex, whose augmentation is 1 (E189). So U_{x²} acts on H^*(G) by N(x)^{-2}, a unit ≡ 1 mod p. The printed argument, which multiplies by the degree N(x)², computes the operator on the restriction of a G-invariant class to Γ^1_0(x), not on H^*(G).
The relation U_x² = U_{x²} is the composition of double cosets at a prime of level Γ_0(x) (ALS.3/hecke-composition).
acceptance: U_{x²} ≡ V_x² mod p.
On the old part spanned by the degeneracy images, U_x has eigenvalues α_x, β_x and U_{x²} has α_x², β_x².
U_{x²} − 1 is invertible on the localization at (m, U_x − α_x) because α_x² ≢ 1.

nodes.title: The Hecke-equivariant Lyndon sequence of the amalgam
nodes.statement: For the amalgam G = Γ^1 ∗_{Γ^1_0(x)} Γ^1 and every m ≥ 1 there is a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^{i−1}(Γ^1_0(x), O/ϖ^m) → H^i(G, O/ϖ^m) → H^i(Γ^1, O/ϖ^m)² → H^i(Γ^1_0(x), O/ϖ^m) → H^{i+1}(G, O/ϖ^m) → ⋯, whose middle map is the difference of the two restrictions (the second through conjugation by g). It is equivariant for U_{x²}, acting on the outer terms as in BT.3/u-x-squared and on H^i(Γ^1)² by the 2 × 2 matrix of Hecke operators induced by the tree endomorphism, and for the Hecke operators prime to x. Localizing at any ideal where U_{x²} − 1 is invertible on all terms gives H^i(Γ^1, O/ϖ^m)²_· ≅ H^i(Γ^1_0(x), O/ϖ^m)_·.
hypotheses: The printed sequence has H^{i−1}(G) where H^i(G) belongs (E190)
Equivariance is asserted without proof in the source (E189); it is proved through the tree
proofSteps: Realize the Lyndon sequence as the Ext_G(−, O/ϖ^m) sequence of the chain complex 0 → C_1(𝒯) → C_0(𝒯) → ℤ → 0 of the Bruhat–Tits tree 𝒯 (ModularCurvesPartII R14.4/lyndon-exact-sequence for the exact sequence).

U_{x²} on H^*(Γ^1_0(x)) is induced by the G-endomorphism of C_1(𝒯) = ℤ[G/Γ^1_0(x)] sending an edge to the sum of the N(x)² edges at distance two; it extends uniquely to a G-endomorphism of C_0(𝒯) compatible with the boundary, inducing the stated 2 × 2 Hecke matrix on the Γ^1-terms.
On H^*(G) the induced endomorphism is the one induced on H_0(𝒯) = ℤ, multiplication by the augmentation 1 of the unnormalized operator, so U_{x²} acts on H^*(G) by N(x)^{-2}, as in BT.3/u-x-squared.

U_{x²} − 1 acts on H^*(G, O/ϖ^m) by the scalar N(x)^{-2} − 1 ∈ pℤ_p (the source claims 0; E189), hence nilpotently; after localizing the sequence (exact, as a sequence of modules over the commutative algebra generated by U_{x²} and the operators prime to x) at an ideal where U_{x²} − 1 is a unit, the H^*(G) terms vanish and the middle map is an isomorphism.
acceptance: The localized isomorphism holds at m̃ = (m, U_x − α_x) since U_{x²} − 1 ≡ α_x² − 1 is a unit there.
At the anaemic m itself the argument does not apply when part of the m-localization has U_x ≡ ±1 (E229).
For F = ℚ this recovers the Ihara-lemma argument of Calegari–Venkatesh Chapter 4.

nodes.title: Lemma 9.6: condition (5) of Conjecture B for n = 2
nodes.statement: Let n = 2, p > 2, Q a set of Taylor–Wiles primes and m a maximal ideal of T^an_{Q,ψ} with B^gal and r̄_m ≅ r̄. For x ∈ Q let α_x, β_x be the two (distinct) eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_x), with α_x the eigenvalue on ψ̄_x. Then for every m ≥ 1 the map (lim_{k→∞}∏_{x∈Q}(V_x − β̃_x)^{k!}) ∘ pr^* , followed by the projection onto the m_Q-part, is an isomorphism H^*_ψ(Y, O/ϖ^m)_m → H^*_ψ(Y_0(Q), O/ϖ^m)_{m_Q}; that is, B^tw(Q, ψ, m) holds.
hypotheses: N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and α_x ≠ β_x (so α_x ≢ ±1, since α_xβ_x ≡ N(x) ≡ 1)
ψ dropped from the notation; the argument is the same for O(ψ) since ψ is trivial at x
Localization at m̃ = (m, U_x − α_x), not at m (E229)
proofSteps: Induction on |Q| reduces to Q = {x}, using that the projectors for different primes commute.

The degeneracy maps φ : H^*(Y)² → H^*(Y_0(x)) and φ^∨ satisfy φ^∨ ∘ φ = (N(x)+1, T_x; T_x, N(x)+1), with determinant (N(x)+1)² − T_x² ∉ m, so H^*(Y_0(x))_m ≅ H^*(Y)²_m ⊕ W and H^*(Y_0(x))_{m̃} ≅ H^*(Y)_{m̃} ⊕ W_{m̃} (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.3/degeneracy-old-forms).

Pass to PSL_2 components (BT.3/psl2-reduction) and apply the localized Lyndon isomorphism at m̃ (BT.3/lyndon-hecke-equivariance), where U_{x²} − 1 ≡ α_x² − 1 is a unit: H^i(Y)²_{m̃} ≅ H^i(Y_0(x))_{m̃}, so W_{m̃} = 0.
Applying the projectors lim(U_x − β̃_x)^{k!} and lim(U_x − α̃_x)^{k!} (exponent k!, E191) identifies H^*(Y)_m with the α_x-part, which is the m_Q-part.
acceptance: For F = ℚ this is the classical 'no new cohomology at Taylor–Wiles level' statement (ModularCurvesPartII R14.4/taylor-wiles-root-control).
The statement concerns all degrees, not only the lowest one (contrast CG18 Remark 9.8).
For n = 3 the method fails: PSL_3(F_x) is not an amalgam of two vertex stabilizers.

sources.match: If n = 2, condition 5 of Conjecture B holds for all Taylor–Wiles primes; proof by degeneracy maps, the amalgam Γ^1 ∗ Γ^1, Lyndon's sequence and U_x² = U_{x²}, completed at m̃ (E229) with k! projectors (E191).
PSL_2(F_x) is an amalgam while PGL_2(F_x) is not; the lowest-degree case is more elementary.

nodes.title: No new cohomology at primes with distinct Frobenius eigenvalues (§9.4)
nodes.statement: Let G = GL_n over F with arithmetic quotients X, X_0(x) (level the line-stabilizer at x), x a prime with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p at which r̄(Frob_x) is unramified with n distinct eigenvalues, α one of them, m_∅ the Hecke ideal away from x and m = (m_∅, V − α) with V the double coset of diag(1, …, 1, ϖ_x). Assume local–global compatibility at x for the localized completed cohomology: every irreducible G(F_x)-subrepresentation of M_j[m_∅], M_j := lim_{m→∞}H^j(X(x^m), O/ϖ^n)_{m_∅}, is the unramified principal series attached to r̄|G_x. Then e_α := lim_k Q(V)^{k!} induces isomorphisms H^*(X, O/ϖ^n)_{m_∅} ≅ H^*(X_0(x), O/ϖ^n)_m, where P(T) = (T − α)Q(T) is the characteristic polynomial of r̄(Frob_x). For the Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_n quotients of §9 the corresponding statement (B^tw at such primes, and the comparison H^i(Y_0(Q), k)_{m_α} ≅ H^i(Y, k)_m that CGH20 Theorem 3.2 uses) is not established here: CG18 only says it should follow from the GL_n case through the central torus fibrations (E194), and it is a recorded gap of this roadmap.
hypotheses: Distinct eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_x) (enormous image supplies such Taylor–Wiles primes)
The local–global compatibility at x is a hypothesis; the source says only 'by assumption'

GL_n quotients are torus bundles (not circle bundles) over PGL_n quotients up to components (E194); the source's remark that the PGL_n case should be easy to deduce is not an argument, and the PGL_n version is the recorded gap 'Distinct-eigenvalue comparison for the Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_n quotients'
proofSteps: Each M_j is filtered by its m_∅-torsion, and the compatibility hypothesis with Ext-vanishing between the unramified principal series and other irreducibles (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5/cg-distinct-block) puts M_j in the block category 𝒞.

Hochschild–Serre for the towers X(x^m) → X and X(x^m) → X_0(x) gives spectral sequences H^i(G(O_x), M_j) ⇒ H^{i+j}(X)_{m_∅} and e_αH^i(U_0(x), M_j) ⇒ H^{i+j}(X_0(x))_m (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.6/finite-cover-hochschild-serre and its tower version).

The map ι_* : H^k(G(O_x), M) → e_αH^k(U_0(x), M) is an isomorphism on the block (SR.5/cg-derived-projector, CG18 Theorem 9.16), so the morphism of spectral sequences is an isomorphism on E_2 and hence on the abutments.

The comparison is equivariant for the Hecke operators away from x. The PGL_n version is not deduced: the torus fibrations of E194 relate the two cohomologies only through a Leray spectral sequence, and Khare–Thorne Lemma 6.25(4), which CGH20 cites, is a GL_n statement at Iwahori level for ordinary completed cohomology (see the gap and sourceIssues E4).
acceptance: For GL_2 with distinct eigenvalues this is the analogue of Lemma 9.6, conditional on local–global compatibility at x; for PGL_2, Lemma 9.6 (BT.3/lemma-9-6) gives B^tw without it.
Without distinct eigenvalues the category 𝒞 is not described by Corollary 9.13 and the argument does not apply.
The isomorphism is compatible with the Hecke operators prime to x.

sources.match: The category 𝒞, the description of its finite-length objects, injectives, and Theorem 9.16 (ι_* is an isomorphism); §9.4.2 applies it to the modules M_j by comparing two Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences.
H^i(Y_0(Q), k)_{m_α} ≅ H^i(Y, k)_m as in §9.4 of CG18 and Khare–Thorne Lemma 6.25(4).

nodes.title: The minimal complexes D̃_N and D̃^χ_N
nodes.statement: For a standing datum, a maximal ideal m of T with r̄_m ≅ r̄, a Taylor–Wiles set Q_N of level N (BT.1/numerical-coincidence) and a surjection Δ̃_{Q_N} ↠ Δ_N := (ℤ/p^N)^q with S_N := O[Δ_N], let Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N) → Y_0(Q_N) be the intermediate covers (0 ≤ M ≤ N). Assuming ConjB(Q_N, ψ, m_{Q_N}) for ψ ∈ {1, χ}, there are perfect complexes D̃_N and D̃^χ_N of finite free S_N-modules (homologically graded) such that: (1) they are concentrated in degrees q_0, …, q_0 + l_0; (2) D̃_N ⊗_{S_N} S_N/𝔪_{S_N} has zero differentials; (3) for every i, n ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ M ≤ N, H_i(D̃_N ⊗_{S_N} S_M/ϖ^n) ≅ e_{Q_N}H_i(Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)_{m^*} and H_i(D̃^χ_N ⊗_{S_N} S_M/ϖ^n) ≅ e_{Q_N}H_{i,χ^{-1}}(Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)_{m^*}, as S_N-modules and compatibly with T^an_{Q_N}; (4) D̃_N ⊗_{S_N} O computes e_{Q_N}H_*(Y_0(Q_N))_{m^*}, which B^tw identifies with H_*(Y)_{m^*}.
hypotheses: Conjecture B at Q_N (vanishing and Taylor–Wiles comparison) for ψ = 1 and ψ = χ
The χ-twisted complex uses the dual local system O(χ^{-1}) (E207)
The projector e_{Q_N} is the Taylor–Wiles projector for the primes of Q_N (E204)
proofSteps: Chains of the cover Y_1(Q_N) form a perfect complex of O[Δ̃_{Q_N}]-modules quasi-isomorphic to the singular chains (Mumford's lemma; ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.1/finite-complex-model), and base change along O[Δ̃] → O[Δ_M]/ϖ^n computes the chains of Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N) with O/ϖ^n coefficients (CG18 Lemma 7.1).

Each Hecke operator lifts to an endomorphism of this perfect complex (CG18 Lemma 7.2; ALS.3/derived-hecke-action), and for the localizing operator t = ∏_{x∈Q_N}P_x ∘ ∏_{i∈Ω}P_i (P_i separating the other residual Galois representations, P_x the Taylor–Wiles projector) the colimit C_t = lim t^k C is a perfect direct summand computing the localized homology (CG18 Lemma 7.3; IHG.2/localizing-operator-summand, IHG.2/factorial-localizing-idempotent).

Over the local ring S_N, Nakayama's lemma for perfect complexes produces a minimal representative D̃_N with zero differentials mod 𝔪_{S_N} and terms of rank dim H_i(Y_0(Q_N), k)_{m^*} (CG18 Lemma 7.4; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7/minimal-representative).

Vanishing outside [q_0, q_0 + l_0] at the residual level (B^van(a) with duality and B^van(b)) bounds the minimal complex to those degrees; B^tw identifies the residual terms with H_*(Y, k)_{m^*}, independent of N.
acceptance: dim_k D̃_{N,i}/𝔪 = dim_k H_i(Y, k)_{m^*} for every N.
For Q_N = ∅ (N = 0), D̃_0 is a minimal complex over O computing H_*(Y, O)_{m^*}.
The minimal representative is unique up to (non-unique) isomorphism of complexes.

The complexes D̃_N and D̃^χ_N: degrees q_0, …, q_0 + l_0, trivial differentials mod 𝔪_{S_N}, homology the projected homology of Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N) localized at m^* (E204, E207).

nodes.title: The two patching data of the proof of Theorem 9.19
nodes.statement: Fix q ≥ h¹_{L^⊥,T}(ad⁰r̄(1)) and Taylor–Wiles sets Q_N (N ≥ 1) as in BT.1/numerical-coincidence, and put g = q + |T| − 1 − [F:ℚ]n(n − 1)/2 − l_0, S_∞ := O⟦(ℤ_p)^q⟧, S_N := O[Δ_N], j := n²|T| − 1, O^□ := O⟦z_1, …, z_j⟧. The datum i = 1 (resp. i = 2) consists of: R^1_∞ := R^1_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧ (resp. R^2_∞ := R^χ_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧); (R^1, H^1) := (R_S, H^{q_0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m) (resp. (R^2, H^2) := (R_{S^χ}, H^{q_0}_χ(Y, K/O)^∨_m)), with R^i acting through BT.2/conj-b-type-s-surjection; the complex T of finite-dimensional k-spaces in degrees 0, …, l_0 with T^c = H^{q_0+l_0−c}(Y, k)^∨_m and zero differentials; D^1_N := D̃_N/ϖ^N and D^2_N := D̃^χ_N/ϖ^N regarded as cohomological complexes in degrees 0, …, l_0 by c ↦ q_0 + l_0 − c; and surjections φ^i_N : R^i_∞ ↠ R^□_{S_{Q_N}} ↠ R_{S_{Q_N}} ↠ R^i (resp. with S^χ), where the surjections R^i_∞ ↠ R^□ are chosen so that their reductions mod ϖ agree under R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ, using representatives of the universal deformations of type S_{Q_N} and S^χ_{Q_N} that agree mod ϖ.
hypotheses: Double brackets for completed rings throughout (Correction items 1, 12; E12, E205)
T^c = H^{q_0+l_0−c}, a reflection of degrees, not a shift by q_0 (E208)
The choice of compatible surjections mod ϖ is needed for the commutative square of the two-datum patching (E209)
proofSteps: R^{□}_{S_{Q_N}} is a quotient of R^1_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧ by BT.1/numerical-coincidence(4); composing with R^□ ≅ R_{S_{Q_N}}⟦z_1, …, z_j⟧ ↠ R_{S_{Q_N}} ↠ R_S gives φ^1_N (BT.1/framing-and-presentation(1)).

For i = 2 take the natural map R^χ_loc → R^□_{S^χ_{Q_N}}, which reduces mod ϖ to the i = 1 map, and send each x_i to a lift of the image of x_i mod ϖ; the resulting map is surjective because it is surjective on reduced cotangent spaces (complete Nakayama).
D^i_N inherits from D̃_N the identification D^i_N ⊗_{S_N} S_N/𝔪 ≅ T (after reflection), since both have zero differentials and the same residual terms.
acceptance: dim R^i_∞ = 1 + q + j − l_0 (BT.1/numerical-coincidence).
For l_0 = 0, T is the single space H^{q_0}(Y, k)^∨_m in degree 0 and the data are those of Taylor–Wiles–Kisin module patching.
R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ by BT.1/local-ring-properties(2) and x_i ↦ x_i.

nodes.title: The patched complexes P^{1,□}_∞ and P^{2,□}_∞
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of BT.4/patching-hypotheses-verified there are perfect complexes P^{1,□}_∞, P^{2,□}_∞ of finitely generated S^□_∞-modules (S^□_∞ = S_∞ ⊗̂ O^□), concentrated in degrees 0, …, l_0, such that for i = 1, 2: (i) P^{i,□}_∞ is a projective resolution of minimal length of H^{l_0}(P^{i,□}_∞); (ii) R^i_∞ ⊗̂_O S^□_∞ acts on H^{l_0}(P^{i,□}_∞), extending the S^□_∞-action, and H^{l_0}(P^{i,□}_∞) is a finite R^i_∞-module; (iii) depth_{R^i_∞} H^{l_0}(P^{i,□}_∞) = 1 + j + q − l_0 = dim R^i_∞; (iv) there are a surjection φ^i_∞ : R^i_∞ ↠ R^i and an isomorphism H^{l_0}(P^{i,□}_∞)/𝔞 ≅ H^i of R^i_∞-modules, 𝔞 = ker(S^□_∞ → O), with the image of 𝔞 in End(H^{l_0}(P^{i,□}_∞)) contained in that of ker φ^i_∞. Moreover there is an isomorphism H^{l_0}(P^{1,□}_∞)/ϖ ≅ H^{l_0}(P^{2,□}_∞)/ϖ of R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ-modules (linear over (R^i_∞ ⊗̂ S^□_∞)/ϖ) compatible with H^1/ϖ ≅ H^2/ϖ after reduction mod 𝔞.
hypotheses: All hypotheses of the two-datum patching theorem, verified in BT.4/patching-hypotheses-verified
H^i ≠ 0, so the complexes are not exact (E130, E134)
proofSteps: Apply the Calegari–Geraghty patching construction to each datum (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8/patched-perfect-complexes-in-a-range-of-degrees): compactness of finite patching data, inverse limit of a compatible tower, the action of R^i_∞ and the augmentation isomorphism.

Patch the two data simultaneously, carrying the comparison isomorphisms mod ϖ as part of each finite datum; this two-datum version (CG18 Proposition 6.6 with the compatibility of E142) is requested from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P8.

dim_{S^□_∞} H^*(P^{i,□}_∞) = dim_{R^i_∞} ≤ dim R^i_∞ = dim S^□_∞ − l_0, so H^* has codimension ≥ l_0 over the regular ring S^□_∞, and the codimension–amplitude lemma (CG18 Lemma 6.2; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P9/balanced-patched-complex) gives (i) and depth = dim S^□_∞ − l_0, which equals the R^i_∞-depth by the patching depth comparison (R03.5/patching-depth-numerical).
acceptance: For l_0 = 0, P^{i,□}_∞ is a single finite free S^□_∞-module (P9/one-degree-specialization).
H^{l_0}(P^{i,□}_∞) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R^i_∞ by (iii).
The comparison mod ϖ is used only through its top-degree part.

nodes.statement: In the situation of BT.5/patched-complexes, H^{l_0}(P^{2,□}_∞) is a nearly faithful R^2_∞-module, and H^{l_0}(P^{1,□}_∞)/ϖ ≅ H^{l_0}(P^{2,□}_∞)/ϖ is nearly faithful over R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ.

R^2_∞ need not be shown p-torsion free: the argument uses depth = dimension (E165)

A finite module of maximal depth over a Noetherian local ring with irreducible spectrum is nearly faithful (Taylor's Lemma 2.3; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6/maximal-cm-nearly-faithful-irreducible).
Near faithfulness passes to the quotient by ϖ (R03.6/nearly-faithful-quotient), and the isomorphism of BT.5/patched-complexes transports it.

If R_triv = ∅ the two sides coincide and this step is not needed.
Near faithfulness is a statement about reduced supports: it gives no integral R = T.

nodes.title: Transfer to the unipotent side and descent to R_S
nodes.statement: In the situation of BT.5/patched-complexes, H^{l_0}(P^{1,□}_∞) is p-torsion free and nearly faithful over R^1_∞, and H^1 = H^{q_0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m is nearly faithful over R^1 = R_S.
hypotheses: R^1_∞ equidimensional with minimal primes of characteristic 0, catenary, and each prime minimal over ϖ contains a unique minimal prime (BT.1/local-ring-properties(1), (4))
proofSteps: Depth = dimension (BT.5/patched-complexes(iii)) forces every associated prime of H^{l_0}(P^{1,□}_∞) to be a minimal prime of R^1_∞ (R03.6/maximal-depth-annihilator-primes-top-dimensional); these have characteristic 0, so ϖ is a nonzerodivisor on the module.

Taylor's Lemma 2.2: a finite module on which ϖ is regular and whose reduction mod ϖ is nearly faithful is nearly faithful, under the stated hypotheses on R^1_∞ (R03.6/nearly-faithful-lift-from-special-fibre), applied with BT.5/chi-side-nearly-faithful.
Conclusion (iv) of BT.5/patched-complexes and the radical comparison transfer near faithfulness from H^{l_0}(P^{1,□}_∞) over R^1_∞ to H^1 over R^1 (R03.6/patching-nearly-faithful-descends).
acceptance: The transfer uses only characteristic-0 minimal primes of R^1_∞, which survives the correction of Lemma 8.2 (E165).
Catenarity holds since R^1_∞ is a quotient of a power series ring over O.
The conclusion is near faithfulness, not faithfulness.

sources.match: Associated primes of H^{l_0}(P^{1,□}_∞) are minimal primes of R^1_∞, of characteristic 0 by Lemma 8.2, so the module is p-torsion free and Taylor's [11, Lemma 2.2] applies; conclusion (iv) gives near faithfulness of H^1 over R_S.

nodes.title: Theorem 9.19: near faithfulness of H^{q_0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m over R_S
nodes.statement: Let (F, n, p, O, r̄, ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2}, R = R_triv ⊔ R_reg, χ) be a standing datum (BT.1/ihara-avoidance-data) with r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) big and F(ad⁰r̄) ∌ ζ_p. Let m be a maximal ideal of T = T_{∅,1} at level K_∅(R) with r̄_m ≅ r̄. Fix q ≥ h¹_{L^⊥,T}(ad⁰r̄(1)) and Taylor–Wiles sets Q_N (N ≥ 1) as in BT.1/numerical-coincidence, and assume ConjB(Q, ψ, m) (BT.2/conjecture-b, including clause (6) and intermediate levels) for Q = ∅ and Q = Q_N, ψ = 1 and ψ = χ. Then H^{q_0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m, regarded as an R_S-module through R_S ↠ T_m, is nearly faithful.
hypotheses: Corrected standing hypotheses: R splits into R_triv (r̄|G_v trivial, Ihara avoidance) and R_reg (single unipotent Jordan block), N(v) ≡ 1 mod p on R (E169, E203)
Conjecture B with the Taylor–Wiles compatibility clause (6) (E181) and at intermediate levels (E1 of this packet)
proofSteps: BT.2/conj-b-type-s-surjection gives R_S ↠ T_m and R_{S^χ} ↠ T_{χ,m}.
BT.4/patching-input-data and BT.4/patching-hypotheses-verified set up and verify the two patching data.
BT.5/patched-complexes produces P^{1,□}_∞, P^{2,□}_∞; BT.5/chi-side-nearly-faithful and BT.5/unipotent-side-nearly-faithful conclude.

For F imaginary quadratic and n = 2 it is conditional on Conjecture B, with B^tw supplied by Lemma 9.6.
Near faithfulness says Spec T_m = Spec R_S on reduced spectra.

Theorem 1.2 is deduced from CG18 Theorems 5.16 and 6.4.

nodes.title: Minimal R = T and freeness when the local rings are smooth
nodes.statement: In the situation of BT.5/theorem-9-19 suppose moreover R_triv = ∅ (every v ∈ R has r̄(σ_v) a single unipotent Jordan block, or R = ∅). Then R_S → T_m is an isomorphism and H^{q_0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m is a free R_S-module; only the datum ψ = 1 is used, and Conjecture B is needed only for ψ = 1.
hypotheses: R_triv = ∅, so R^1_loc is formally smooth over O (BT.1/cg-local-rings)
Conjecture B for Q = ∅ and Q = Q_N with ψ = 1
proofSteps: R^1_∞ = R^1_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧ is a power series ring over O, hence regular and p-torsion free.
Patching the single datum i = 1 (BT.5/patched-complexes for one datum) gives H^{l_0}(P^{1,□}_∞) of depth dim R^1_∞, hence free by Auslander–Buchsbaum (R03.6/patching-free-conclusion).

Freeness and conclusion (iv) give ker φ_∞ = ı(𝔞)R^1_∞ and H^1 free over R_S (R03.6/patching-kernel-equals-ideal, R03.6/patched-module-r-equals-t); since R_S acts on H^1 through T_m, R_S ≅ T_m (R03.6/r-equals-t-of-free).

Then T_m is a complete intersection.
If R_triv ≠ ∅ only near faithfulness is obtained.

R ≅ T is obtained from CG18 Theorems 5.16 and 6.4 because the local deformation rings (minimal at the Steinberg places, Fontaine–Laffaille at p) are formally smooth.

nodes.title: Cuspidal recognition of the support of H^{q_0}(Y)_m
nodes.statement: Let m be a maximal ideal of T at level K_∅(R) at which B^gal and B^van hold for Q = ∅, ψ = 1, with r̄_m absolutely irreducible and r̄_m(G_{F(ζ_p)}) big. Fix ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. If f : T_m → Q̄_p is an O-algebra map such that the f-eigenspace of H^{q_0}(Y, Q̄_p)_m is nonzero, then there is a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with trivial central character and trivial infinitesimal character at every archimedean place, with (π^∞)^{K_∅(R)} ≠ 0, whose unnormalized Hecke eigenvalues are ι f(T_{λ,i}) for every λ ∉ S.
hypotheses: Boundary vanishing B^van(b) at m
Bigness of r̄_m(G_{F(ζ_p)}) (CHT Definition 2.5.1), used to exclude residual eigensystems
Eisenstein (non-discrete) eigensystems of H^*(Y, ℂ) occur in boundary cohomology: requested from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.5
proofSteps: B^van(b) with coefficients K (universal coefficients from O/ϖ^m) gives H^*(∂Y, K)_m = 0, so H^{q_0}(Y, ℂ)_m consists of interior classes (ALS.4/boundary-triangle).

The f-eigenclass is realized by an isobaric automorphic representation Π from a summand of the Franke–Schwermer decomposition (AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.5/isobaric-realization; ALS.5/automorphic-comparison).

If Π comes from a non-discrete (Eisenstein) contribution, its eigensystem occurs in H^*(∂Y, ℂ) (requested from AS.5), contradicting the first step. If Π is residual, the Moeglin–Waldspurger classification (requested from AS.4) gives Π = Speh(σ, k) with k ≥ 2.

In the residual case, at every λ ∉ S with N(λ) ≡ 1 mod p the Hecke polynomial of Π_λ is a product ∏_{j<k}P_σ(N(λ)^{−j}cX) whose roots reduce mod ϖ with multiplicity ≥ k; by Chebotarev (Tau Ceti Chebotarev layer 10) every element of r̄_m(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is some r̄_m(Frob_λ) with N(λ) ≡ 1 mod p, contradicting bigness, which provides an element with a simple eigenvalue.

Hence Π = π is cuspidal; trivial coefficients give trivial infinitesimal character, and π_∞ is tempered by Clozel's purity lemma (AF.4/clozel-purity), consistent with degree q_0 (AF.4/borel-wallach-tempered-range).
acceptance: For F = ℚ and n = 2 this is the statement that non-Eisenstein classes in H^1 of a modular curve come from cusp forms.
Without bigness, a Speh(σ, 2) eigensystem is not excluded by this argument.
The passage from a point of R_S to π is not written in the source (it says Theorem 5.16 follows immediately from Theorem 9.19; E3 of this packet).

sources.locator: Theorem 5.16 and the sentence after it, published pp. 383–384
sources.match: Modularity means a regular algebraic cusp form π with trivial infinitesimal character and L(r, s) = L(π, s); the deduction from Theorem 9.19 is not written.
Boundary vanishing after localization, the input the brief names for passing to a cuspidal π.

Eigenclasses in cohomology are realized by isobaric automorphic representations (Franke's Theorem 2.3); a class outside the tempered range [q_0, q_0 + l_0] forces the representation to be non-tempered (Borel–Wallach and Clozel's Lemma 3.14), which strong multiplicity one then contradicts.

nodes.title: The maximal ideal m from hypothesis (8)
nodes.statement: Let r̄ be the residual representation of a standing datum. (a) If π_0 is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) with trivial central character and trivial infinitesimal character, unramified at every v | p and outside S, with π_{0,v}^{Iw(v)} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R, whose unnormalized Hecke eigenvalues at λ ∉ S (after ι : ℂ ≅ Q̄_p) are integral and reduce to the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of r̄(Frob_λ) in the convention of BT.2/conj-b-galois-type, then there is a maximal ideal m of T at level K_∅(R) with H^{q_0}(Y, k)_m ≠ 0 and r̄_m ≅ r̄ (given B^gal at m). (b) If r̄ is Serre modular of minimal level and R = R(r̄), such an m exists by definition (BT.0/serre-modular-minimal-level).
hypotheses: (a) uses Clozel's purity lemma and the Borel–Wallach range to place π_0 in cuspidal cohomology in degree q_0
Uniqueness of r̄_m is Chebotarev with Brauer–Nesbitt
proofSteps: π_{0,∞} is tempered and cohomological for the trivial coefficient system (AF.4/clozel-purity, AF.4/borel-wallach-tempered-range), so π_0 contributes to H^{q_0}_cusp(Y(K_∅(R)), ℂ) (ALS.5/cuspidal-cohomology), since (π_0^∞)^{K_∅(R)} ≠ 0.

T acts on the finite O-module H^{q_0}(Y, O) and its eigensystem on the π_0-part is integral; reduction gives a maximal ideal m in the support of H^{q_0}(Y, O), hence of H^{q_0}(Y, k) by Nakayama and universal coefficients.
The Hecke polynomials at m are the reductions of those of π_0, i.e. the characteristic polynomials of r̄(Frob_λ); so r̄_m ≅ r̄ by IHG.3/galois-type-maximal-ideal (uniqueness).
(b) is the definition.
acceptance: In (a) the paper's hypothesis that the p-adic representation r_p(π_0) exists and satisfies condition (6) is replaced by the eigenvalue congruence and Iwahori-sphericity at R, which make sense over every number field (E2 of this packet).
For F totally real or CM, (a) follows from the paper's form through the Galois representations attached to π_0 and local–global compatibility at ℓ ≠ p.
The ideal m depends only on r̄, not on π_0.
