The proof assumes a maximal ideal m of T = T_{∅,1} with r̄_m ≅ r̄; producing m from (8a) or (8b) is left to the reader (brief, item thm-5-16).

nodes.title: Theorem 5.16: conditional modularity lifting for GL_n over any number field
nodes.statement: Assume Conjecture B for F (BT.2/conjecture-b, with clause (6) and intermediate levels). Let F be a number field, n ≥ 2, p > n a prime unramified in F, O as in BT.1/ihara-avoidance-data, and r : G_F → GL_n(O) continuous and unramified outside a finite set, with reduction r̄. Suppose: (1) r|G_v is crystalline for v | p; (2) for v | p, gr^i(r ⊗_{ℤ_p} B_dR)^{G_v} is free of rank one over O ⊗_{ℤ_p} F_v for i ∈ {0, …, n − 1} and zero otherwise; (3) r̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible and F(ad⁰r̄) ∌ ζ_p; (4) r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big (CHT Definition 2.5.1); (5) r is odd at every real place; (6′) for every finite place x ∤ p at which r (or, in case (8a), π_0) is ramified: r|I_x is unipotent, and either r̄|G_x is trivial and N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, or r̄|I_x is unipotent with r̄(σ_x) a single Jordan block; (7) det r = ε^{n(n−1)/2}; (8) either (a) there is π_0 as in BT.5/maximal-ideal-from-hypothesis-8(a) for R the set of places in (6′), or (b) r̄ is Serre modular of minimal level and r is ramified only at places where r̄ is ramified. Then r is modular: there is a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with trivial central character and trivial infinitesimal character such that, for every finite place λ ∤ p outside the set R of places in (6′), π_λ is unramified and the characteristic polynomial of r(Frob_λ) (arithmetic Frobenius) is Σ_i (−1)^i N(λ)^{i(i−1)/2} t_{λ,i}(π) X^{n−i}, t_{λ,i}(π) the unnormalized Hecke eigenvalues of π_λ; equivalently, with arithmetic Frobenius in the Euler factors of L(r, s), L^S(r, s) = L^S(π, s − (n − 1)/2) for S = S_p ∪ R.
hypotheses: (6′) corrects the printed (6) and (8a) (E125, E169; E2 of this packet): where r̄ is unramified it adds that r̄|G_x is trivial (Taylor's Ihara avoidance), where r̄ is ramified it asks for a single Jordan block (the minimally ramified ring), and it keeps the printed proviso that N(x) ≡ 1 mod p is needed only where r̄ is unramified; the deletion of that proviso proposed in E203 is not needed once the ramified places of r̄ use the minimally ramified ring
(4) is bigness of r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) (E126)
Conjecture B is a hypothesis; for n = 2 its condition (5) holds by Lemma 9.6
proofSteps: Put R := the places of (6′), R_triv := those with r̄|G_x trivial, R_reg := the rest. By (1)–(3), (5)–(7) and Fontaine–Laffaille theory (p > n, F unramified at p), (F, n, p, O, r̄, ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2}, R, χ) is a standing datum for any choice of χ (BT.1/ihara-avoidance-data); in case (8b), R = R(r̄).
BT.5/maximal-ideal-from-hypothesis-8 gives m with r̄_m ≅ r̄ at level K_∅(R).
BT.1/numerical-coincidence gives Taylor–Wiles sets Q_N; BT.5/theorem-9-19 gives near faithfulness of H := H^{q_0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m over R_S.

By BT.1/lift-has-type-s, r gives x_r : R_S → O; near faithfulness puts ker x_r in Supp_{R_S} H, so H ⊗_{R_S,x_r} K ≠ 0. Pontryagin duality and B^van(a) identify H ⊗ K with the K-dual of H^{q_0}(Y, K)_m, so the eigensystem x_r of T_m occurs in H^{q_0}(Y, K)_m.

BT.5/cuspidal-recognition turns this eigensystem into a cuspidal π; Chebotarev and the Hecke polynomial convention (IHG.3/gln-hecke-polynomial) give the stated equality of characteristic polynomials and of partial L-functions.
acceptance: For n = 2 and F imaginary quadratic, Conjecture B(5) is Lemma 9.6 (BT.3/lemma-9-6) and (4)(a) is BT.2/conj-b-small-rank(1).
For F = ℚ and n = 2 the theorem is unconditional and is the Taylor–Wiles/Taylor Ihara-avoidance modularity lifting theorem in weight two at Fontaine–Laffaille primes.

The theorem is exported to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 as a conditional endpoint, through CG18 Theorem 1.1 (potential modularity of elliptic curves over any number field, assuming Conjecture B).

requests.need: Rank-n Taylor–Wiles primes under bigness, in the form of CHT Proposition 2.5.9 adapted to unpolarized GL_n with fixed determinant ξ (CG18 Proposition 8.5(1)–(3), pp. 410–411): for a number field F, p > n, r̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) absolutely irreducible with r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) big and F(ad⁰r̄) ∌ ζ_p, a finite set T of places containing S_p, local conditions L_v at T, and q ≥ h¹_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad⁰r̄(1)), for every N ≥ 1 a set Q of q places disjoint from T with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p^N, r̄|G_x = s̄_x ⊕ ψ̄_x with ψ̄_x a one-dimensional generalized Frobenius eigenspace, and H¹_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad⁰r̄(1)) = 0 for the Taylor–Wiles local conditions of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2/taylor-wiles-local-tangent at Q.

The big-subgroup condition of CHT Definition 2.5.1 for H ⊂ GL_n(k) (no nontrivial p-power quotient; H⁰ and H¹ of H with coefficients in ad⁰ vanish; every irreducible k[H]-submodule W of gl_n contains, for some h ∈ H with a simple eigenvalue α, an element with nonzero trace against the α-eigenprojector of h), with its invariance under extension of k and the consequence that a big subgroup contains an element with a simple eigenvalue.

BLGHT (Calabi–Yau II) Lemma 3.3 in C_O: completed tensor products over O of complete local O-algebras that are equidimensional with characteristic-0 minimal primes are equidimensional of dimension the sum of relative dimensions plus one, with characteristic-0 minimal primes; after enlarging O so that components are geometrically irreducible, the irreducible components of the tensor product are the products of components, and the property 'each prime minimal over ϖ contains a unique minimal prime' is preserved.

The two-datum version of P8/patched-perfect-complexes-in-a-range-of-degrees (CG18 Proposition 6.6, pp. 390–391) with the compatibility hypothesis recorded in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 E142: given two data satisfying the hypotheses of that node, with R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ, R^1/ϖ ≅ R^2/ϖ, H^1/ϖ ≅ H^2/ϖ and, for M ≥ N ≥ 0, isomorphisms of top-degree cohomology H^{l_0}(D^1_M ⊗ S_N/ϖ) ≅ H^{l_0}(D^2_M ⊗ S_N/ϖ) that become R_∞ ⊗ S^□_N/ϖ-linear after framing and reduce for N → 0 to the given comparison with H/ϖ, the patched complexes carry an isomorphism H^{l_0}(P^1_∞)/ϖ ≅ H^{l_0}(P^2_∞)/ϖ linear over (R_∞ ⊗̂ S^□_∞)/ϖ and compatible with H^1/ϖ ≅ H^2/ϖ modulo 𝔞.

For Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_n over any number field and trivial (or algebraic) coefficients: a Hecke eigensystem of H^*(Y(K), ℂ) whose Franke–Schwermer realization (AS.5/isobaric-realization) comes from a summand with cuspidal support {P} ≠ {G} either occurs in H^*(∂Y(K), ℂ) or is the eigensystem of a residual (discrete-spectrum) automorphic representation.

The Moeglin–Waldspurger description of the residual spectrum of GL_n over a number field: every residual discrete automorphic representation is Speh(σ, k) for k | n, k ≥ 2, σ cuspidal on GL_{n/k}, with unramified local components having Satake parameters {s_i q^{(k−1)/2 − j}} (the existing node AS.4/yu-020 treats the everywhere-unramified function-field case).

The local Artin map Art_v with its normalization (uniformizers to arithmetic Frobenius), used to transport inertial characters to Iwahori characters and diamond operators.

gaps.detail: PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 routes to this roadmap the comparison H^i(Y_0(Q), k)_{m_α} ≅ H^i(Y, k)_m for the Res_{F/ℚ}PGL_n quotients of CG18 §9, at sets Q of primes with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and distinct eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_x) (CGH20 Theorem 3.2 = A.4, proof). CG18 §9.4 proves the analogue for GL_n arithmetic quotients under local–global compatibility at x (BT.3/distinct-eigenvalue-comparison) and only says that the PGL_n case should follow; Khare–Thorne Lemma 6.25(4), which CGH20 also cites, concerns GL_n over CM fields at Iwahori level and ordinary completed cohomology (sourceIssues E4). Two routes are open: rerun §9.4 for smooth PGL_n(F_x)-modules (GL_n(F_x)-modules with trivial central character) with the block theory of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.5 and the derived comparison for the images of GL_n(O_x) and U_0(x) in PGL_n(F_x); or compare the GL_n and PGL_n cohomologies through the central torus fibrations (E194 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18) by a Leray argument after localization at a non-Eisenstein m. Neither is in the sources. The end theorems of this roadmap do not use it, because B^tw is a hypothesis of Theorem 9.19; its consumer is AdjointSelmerGroupsFromModularityLifting (CGH20 Theorem A.4).
